subject: Compiler-aligned WVB 1.38 registered Foreign-call containment
claim: Implementation commit 1e12b2f24f42a121a0d10c6e908592d15bbd4b9a makes the Windows source-built compiler-aligned verifier accept the exact registered WVB 1.38 Foreign call, enforce typed and affine pointer containment, reject ten focused mutations, and keep every execution consumer closed.

runs.target: Authenticated WVB 1.38 publication, complete compiler verification, mutation containment, deterministic publication, and closed execution boundary

limitations: The focused oracle covered 21 production-ingress cases, including canonical complete verification, seven structural WVB mutations, and three typed or affine operand substitutions; it was not the complete changed-file development plan.
The verifier proves exact operand types and affine pointer availability. The provider must still compare the expected generation value with live state at runtime.
The published front door, scalar provider, native lowerer, launchers, browser, WebAssembly, package, and operating-system consumers still reject WVB 1.38.
No native address or symbol was resolved, no Foreign function executed, and no capability or library authority was granted.
The run is local Windows development evidence and does not claim Linux reproduction, paired-host conformance, qualification, release, or independent reproduction.

The broader changed-file plan selected unrelated inherited runtime and library owners because shared verifier files are conservatively routed; those deliberately closed consumers were not rerun for this verification-only checkpoint.
